sources.title: Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1 model card
sources.evidence: Names the exact v1 model, NVIDIA developer, Nemotron family, April 7, 2025 release, nominal 253B size, dense architecture, text input/output, 131,072-token limit, reasoning toggle, tool calling and license. Reopened October 27, 2026: current repository remains at this pinned revision; the architecture section explicitly states 253B model parameters and describes NAS/FFN structural changes. No active count is stated.

sources.title: Ultra 253B v1 checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: DeciLMForCausalLM/nemotron-nas, hidden size 16,384, vocabulary 128,256, untied embeddings, BF16, 162 configured slots, 64 attention blocks and 81 FFNs; context 131,072. All retained attention uses 128 query heads with groups of 16; all sparsify/linear-replacement settings are disabled. Reopened October 27, 2026; hidden_size=16384, num_attention_heads=128 and num_hidden_layers=162 are unchanged.

sources.title: Ultra 253B v1 model implementation
sources.evidence: Defines every learned projection, embedding and RMSNorm tensor. No-op blocks instantiate no corresponding parameters; FFN widths round int(2*ffn_mult*hidden_size/3) upward to a multiple of 256. RoPE inverse frequencies are nonpersistent buffers.

sources.title: Ultra 253B v1 BF16 checkpoint index and referenced shard headers
sources.evidence: Index maps 647 named weight tensors to 49 shards and records 506,802,536,448 data bytes. Bounded HTTP Range reads of every referenced shard header independently found 253,401,268,224 BF16 elements, all learned weights; no quantization scales or persistent buffers. October 27 parameter re-audit reopened only the index and reconfirmed total_size=506802536448; the earlier header census is preserved, not repeated.

sources.title: Llama-Nemotron: Efficient Reasoning Models, revision 5
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026, including full fresh cached text. The September 2025 revision explicitly identifies Ultra 253B v1. Section 2 documents attention removal, variable FFN widths and additional Ultra FFN fusion, so a 405B base active count cannot transfer. Section 5.2.2 uses nominal 253B for BF16 memory accounting; Section 7.4 and Table 5 evaluate Ultra. No separate active-parameter count or activated-parameter comparison column was found.

sources.title: Nemotron Super 120B vs Ultra 253B: NVIDIA’s Best Open-Weight Models Benchmarked
sources.evidence: Read October 27, 2026 as a later original benchmark lead. The April 14, 2026 What We Tested table lists exact nvidia/Llama-3_1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1 BF16 and FP8 rows with Active Params 253B. Not adopted: the publisher’s companion model specification contradicts the original checkpoint dimensions and release date, weakening confidence in its parameter convention; no reliable NVIDIA or model-research comparison independently establishing the claim was found in the inspected sources.

sources.title: InferenceBench Nemotron Ultra 253B specification, rejected corroboration
sources.evidence: Read October 27, 2026 to check the s10 lead. Lists active 253B but also 96 layers, hidden size 12288, 96 query heads and March 18, 2025 release. NVIDIA’s pinned config instead has 162 configured slots, hidden size 16384 and 128 query heads, and its card identifies April 7 release. The active claim is therefore not accepted as reliable specification evidence.

parameter_count_reproduction.method: Reconstruct all parameter shapes from pinned config.json and modeling_decilm.py, compare their names with the complete checkpoint index, then sum shape products from HTTP 206 Range bytes=0-65535 responses for all 49 safetensors shards. Only headers were read; no full weight shards were downloaded.
parameter_count_reproduction.formula: H=16384; V=128256. Untied embedding and output: 2*V*H. Each retained attention block: 2*H*H+2*H*(H/16), plus H RMSNorm weights. Each retained FFN: 3*H*I plus H RMSNorm weights, where I=ceil(int(2*ffn_mult*H/3)/256)*256. Add final H RMSNorm weights. No-op sublayers add zero.
parameter_count_reproduction.non_parameter_accounting: All 647 indexed tensors are .weight parameters instantiated by the implementation. There are no scale tensors or packed quantized elements in this BF16 checkpoint. RoPE inv_freq is a nonpersistent buffer and is absent from the checkpoint and learned-parameter sum.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains the precise 253.401268224B learned checkpoint total, freshly corroborated by unchanged repository metadata and index bytes, alongside NVIDIA’s nominal 253B specification. Reopened the exact card/config, revised technical report, release post and March 2026 NVIDIA QAD comparison; targeted later active-count searches yielded no reliable separate count. Rejected InferenceBench’s explicit 253B-active lead because its companion model specifications contradict NVIDIA’s configuration. Active parameters remain undisclosed, with no dense-equals-total or structurally changed base inference. All 12 unrelated field assessments and the prior parameter reproduction are preserved.
